column2: You push the change up. It's adopted Air Force-wide.
The bureaucracy stalls it for a year.
One of your PJs did something truly heroic under fire. {co} wants to downgrade the award to save paperwork. What do you do?
Push for it
He receives the higher award. Deserved.
Denied. {co} is annoyed with you.
Accept the downgrade
The PJ gets the lesser award. He notices.
A new rescue hoist failed twice in testing. Program managers want you to sign off on fielding it. What's your recommendation?
Don't field it
The flaw is fixed first. Nobody falls.
Sign off
It works fine in the field.
It fails during a real rescue. People get hurt.
Rockets hit your base and fighters breach the perimeter. Your PJs are medics, but they're also trained shooters. How do you employ them?
Treat casualties
Your PJs run a casualty collection point. Nobody who reaches them dies.
Reinforce the perimeter
Your team helps throw back the attack.
You're hit by shrapnel on the wall.
Rescue Group Command
As {rank}, you command a rescue group. Budget planners want to cut a Pave Hawk squadron. You're asked to testify. What's your angle?
Bring a rescued pilot
He tells his story. The room goes silent. Funding saved.
Moving testimony. The cut happens anyway.
Hard data
Eyes glaze over at slide 40.
Future wars may not have air superiority. Slow helicopters may not survive. How do you reshape rescue doctrine?
Small, hidden teams
Your 'survive and wait' concept becomes doctrine.
Critics call it abandoning pilots.
Push for new aircraft
Faster rescue aircraft get funded.
A decade-long acquisition fight begins.
After 28 years, your body is a collection of old injuries. You could retire, or take one last command tour. What do you do?
Your retirement ceremony is packed with people you rescued.
One more tour
Your knees file a formal complaint.
Wall of Names
You're dedicating a new memorial to pararescuemen killed in action. Families are in the front row. What do you say?
Read every name
It takes 20 minutes. Nobody moves.
Tell one story
You tell how one of them died saving a stranger. Everyone feels it.
Failed Rescue News
A rescue under your command failed, and the pilot died. A news outlet is running the story tomorrow. How do you respond?
Full transparency
You explain what went wrong. The family respects it.
Speculation fills the void. It gets worse.
Young Officer Asks
A new lieutenant asks you for the single most important thing about leading PJs. What do you tell her?
'Take care of your people'
She writes it down. Years later, she's a great commander.
'Never stop training'
She becomes famous for brutal, realistic training.
At a NATO rescue conference, allies propose shared rescue procedures. Some of your staff worry about security. What do you do?
Champion it
Allied crews can now rescue each other seamlessly.
Classification fights stall it.
Proceed cautiously
Slow progress, no leaks.
A respected senior chief in your group is accused of harassing a junior airman. He's a legend. What do you do?
Full investigation
Facts come out. Justice is done either way.
It goes away.
It doesn't go away. Now it's about you too.
Half your group's helicopters are grounded for parts. Readiness reports look terrible. What do you do?
Push the maintainers
Slight improvement, very tired maintainers.
Escalate for funding
Emergency parts funding approved.
Denied. 'Do more with less.'
A retired PJ you once led calls at 2 AM. He's drinking and talking about the patients he lost. What do you do?
Drive to his house
You sit with him until sunrise. He gets help that week.
Give him the crisis line
He says thanks. You worry for weeks.
At Thanksgiving, your aunt asks if you're a pilot. You try to explain pararescue for the fifth year in a row. What do you say?
Explain again
She nods. She still thinks you're a pilot.
'Yes, I'm a pilot'
Easier. More pie.
At a school career day, a kid asks what a PJ actually does. What do you tell him?
'I save people'
He says he wants to do it too.
'I jump out of planes'
The whole class loses its mind.
There's an open-water memorial swim for fallen PJs this weekend. It's cold and three miles. Will you join?
Swim it
Freezing, painful, meaningful.
Donate instead
The foundation thanks you.
A guy at the base pool challenges you to a 400-meter race. He looks suspiciously fit. Do you accept?
You win by a body length.
He swam in college. You lose badly.
You keep your mystique.
Bad Rescue Movie
The team watches a rescue movie where the hero does CPR on a conscious man. {buddy} is losing his mind. Do you join?
Heckle the screen
Enjoy it quietly
It's fun if you turn off your brain.
A&S Day One
Assessment and Selection starts with a ruck run in the North Carolina heat. Half the class looks like they already regret it. How do you start?
Set a hard pace
You finish near the front. A cadre member writes something down.
You blow up at mile six and limp in at the back.
Stay steady, mid-pack
You finish strong and unremarkable. In A&S, that's a win.
Help a struggling candidate
Cadre notice you carrying someone else's water. Team players get remembered.
You both come in late. Nobody remembers why.
The Unknown Distance
The cadre won't say how far today's ruck is. It's been four hours. Rumor says it never ends. What's your mindset?
You stop counting and keep moving. Turns out it was 18 miles.
Your feet bleed through your socks but you finish. Barely.
Ask a cadre how far
He actually tells you. You're stunned.
'As far as it takes, candidate.' He writes your number down.
Consider dropping (DOR)
You think about it hard, then don't. The doubt costs you, though.
A psychologist asks why you want to be a Raider and how you handle failure. Your answer could decide your career. What do you say?
Honest and humble
You talk about your failures plainly. The psych nods. Good sign.
You ramble. The psych's face gives nothing away.
Somehow it lands.
'So you want to be in a movie?' Not great.
Talk about your team
You say Raiders are a team sport. The board loves it.
It sounds rehearsed because it is.
Team Event Sandbag
Your A&S team must carry a waterlogged log and sandbags across a swamp. Your teammate {buddy} keeps letting go. How do you handle it?
Quietly pick up his slack
Cadre see you take more weight without complaining.
Your back tweaks under the extra load.
Call him out loudly
He grips tighter. It works, but he hates you.
The cadre mark you as a poor teammate.
Rotate positions
You organize a rotation. Leadership noticed.
The rotation falls apart in the mud.
Your name is read at the end of A&S. You're going to the Individual Training Course. A cadre shakes your hand. How do you celebrate?
Your mom cries. Your dad pretends he isn't.
Eat everything in sight
You eat three burgers and a whole pizza. No regrets.
Sleep for 14 hours
You wake up still in your boots.
ITC Close Quarters
Shoot house day at ITC. You're number two through the door, and the room has hostages and targets mixed together. What's your approach?
Fast and aggressive
Clean hits, zero hostages tagged. Instructor grunts approval.
You put two rounds into a hostage target. Long debrief.
Controlled and deliberate
Slower, but perfect. That's what they want.
Too slow. The number one man is clearing your corner.
Follow the man in front
You flow off him smoothly.
You both end up looking at the same corner.
You're 'captured' during SERE training. The interrogator is very convincing and you haven't slept in a day. How do you hold up?
Stick to the code
You give nothing beyond what's allowed. You'll never forget this week.
You say something you shouldn't have. Instructors note it.
Crack a joke
The interrogator almost smiles.
He does not find you funny. More stress positions.
Go silent
Silence works. You survive.
Silence made them work harder on you.
ITC assigns you a language for foreign internal defense work. Classes run late after long days. How hard do you study?
Flashcards every night
You can order food and ask for a village elder. Progress.
You're exhausted and still mixing up verbs.
Bare minimum
You pass. Barely. Interpreters will love you.
Practice with a native speaker
A local shop owner becomes your tutor. Huge improvement.
He mostly teaches you slang and insults.
An old instructor tells you about the 1942 Makin Island raid, launched from submarines. He asks what 'Spiritus Invictus' means to you. Your answer?
Unconquerable spirit
He nods. 'Now earn it.'
Never quit
'Close enough,' he says. 'Don't forget it.'
He stares at you until you feel very small.
The Raider Pin
ITC graduation. You're now a Critical Skills Operator. {buddy} pins you and grins. What do you do afterward?
Toast the fallen Raiders
Your team raises a glass in silence. It hits harder than you expected.
Party in Jacksonville
Great night, nothing broken, nobody arrested.
A bar fight on graduation night. Your commander is not impressed.
Fly home
Your hometown treats you like a celebrity for a weekend.
New Guy Duties
You're the new guy on your team in {unit}. Someone has to clean the team room, inventory gear, and make coffee. Guess who. Your attitude?
Do it without a word
Senior guys notice. The coffee is also good.
Complain in the group chat
Everyone saw it. Including the team chief.
You turn inventory into a game. Even the old guys join.
Nobody plays. You still do it alone.
You're slotted for combat diver training. Pool comp is legendary: instructors rip off your regulator underwater. How do you face it?
Stay calm, fix it
You methodically untangle everything. Pass.
You panic and bolt for the surface. Fail.
Train extra beforehand
Weeks of breath holds pay off. Smooth pass.
You overtrain and arrive exhausted.
Ask to delay the course
You get a later slot. Someone else takes yours.
Jump School Mishap
On a static line jump, your canopy twists and you're spinning. The ground is coming fast. What do you do?
Bicycle kick out
The twists unwind. You land with a story.
You land hard and wreck your ankle.
Pull the reserve
Reserve opens. Rough landing, but you walk away.
Both canopies tangle. You hit hard.
The canopy fixes itself. Pure luck.
killed in a parachute malfunction
You hit the ground like a sack of bricks.
Range Brass Detail
After a 3,000-round day, someone has to police brass in the rain. {buddy} suggests hiding a few bags behind the berm. What do you do?
Pick it all up
Soaked and miserable, but honest.
Hide the brass
Nobody checks. You go home early.
Range control finds it. Everyone gets smoked, then you get NJP.
Talk him out of it
He rolls his eyes, but helps.
Your Marine Special Operations Team deploys to {country} to train local forces. On the plane, {buddy} asks if you're nervous. Your answer?
He admits he is too. You both feel better.
'Born ready'
He laughs. 'Sure, new guy.'
Sleep the whole flight
Pro move. You land rested.
Partner Force Range
You're teaching marksmanship to partner soldiers in {country}. One keeps sweeping the line with his muzzle. How do you correct him?
Calm demonstration
He gets it. Nobody dies today.
He nods and keeps doing it.
Yell like a drill instructor
It works, through translation.
He's humiliated in front of his unit. Rapport drops.
Have his sergeant fix it
Letting their leaders lead is the whole point of FID.
His sergeant shrugs. It's a long day.
Tea With the Elder
A village elder in {country} invites you for tea. It's your third cup and your stomach is not okay. Refusing could be rude. What do you do?
Drink it
Strong rapport. He shares useful information.
You spend two days hugging a latrine.
He understands. Mostly.
He's offended. The meeting ends early.
Fake sipping
Nobody notices. Diplomacy achieved.
His grandson notices. Awkward.
Your patrol takes fire from a tree line in {country}. Partner forces scatter. {buddy} is pinned behind a low wall. What do you do?
Lay down covering fire
{buddy} sprints to cover. The enemy breaks contact.
A round finds you as you rise up to shoot.
Rally the partner force
You get them firing back. The ambush collapses.
You get hit running between positions.
Call for support
Mortars land on the tree line. Contact over.
Support is 30 minutes out. It's a long 30 minutes.
Night Vision Fail
Your NVG battery dies halfway through a night movement. It's pitch black and silence is critical. What now?
Swap batteries by feel
You practiced this blindfolded. It pays off.
You drop the spare. It's gone forever.
Grab the man ahead's pack
You follow by touch. Embarrassing but effective.
Use a flashlight
Nobody saw it. You got lucky.
The whole team hisses at you. Never again.
On a foot patrol, you spot disturbed dirt and a wire near the path. The team is 20 meters behind you. What do you do?
Freeze and call it out
EOD confirms an IED. You may have saved lives.
It's a buried cable. Better safe than sorry.
Inspect it yourself
Just trash. You got lucky.
It detonates.
Detour around
You reroute safely.
The detour had a second device.
Morning PT Smoke
Your team chief runs a PT session that leaves everyone puking. {buddy} says you should complain to the officer. What do you do?
Suck it up
Next week, you're the one not puking.
The officer laughs and tells the chief. The next PT is worse.
Ask the chief to program it
He's impressed you care. You help plan PT now.
'You want programming? Do burpees.'
Liberty in Okinawa
On a stopover in Okinawa, {buddy} wants to hit Gate 2 Street after curfew. The liberty rules are strict. Do you go?
You hear the next morning that a bunch of guys got caught.
Go out
Best night of the deployment.
Shore patrol catches you after curfew. NJP.
You get back in time. Responsible fun.
The taxi gets lost. You're 10 minutes late.
You want to post a photo of your kit and team on social media. It looks very cool. What do you do?
Post it
The team's faces are visible. OPSEC brief, in person, loudly.
Blur faces and post
Gets a ton of likes and no trouble.
The geotag showed your base. Oops.
Don't post it
Smart. The best operators are boring online.
Sniper Course Slot
One slot is open for a sniper course. You and {buddy} both want it. The team chief asks you to make your case. What do you do?
Show your range data
Your numbers win. You get the slot.
His numbers are better.
He never forgets it. Next slot is yours.
Badmouth him
You get it. He knows what you did.
The chief sees right through it.
During a sniper stalk, an instructor walks within three feet of your ghillie suit. Your nose itches terribly. What do you do?
Don't move at all
He walks past. You take your shot. Pass.
He spots the barrel glint anyway.
Scratch very slowly
Somehow, you get away with it.
'Got you.' The instructor taps your head.
Injury at Training
You tear something in your shoulder during fast-rope training. Reporting it could cost you a deployment. What do you do?
Surgery and rehab. You'll be back.
It heals on its own. You dodged a bullet.
It fully tears on deployment. Now it's surgery and a long rehab.
Ask the team corpsman quietly
He sets you up with a physical therapy plan.
He reports it anyway. Medical hold.
Fast Rope Burn
Fast-roping from a hovering helicopter at night, your gloves start smoking. The ground's about 20 feet down. What do you do?
Grip tighter
Your palms sting but you land fine.
You burn through and drop the last 10 feet.
Use your boots more
Textbook. You land soft.
Your feet slip. Rough landing.
Surprise room inspection. Your roommate {buddy} has energy drinks and protein powder all over the floor. What's your move?
Speed clean his mess
You pass with seconds to spare. He owes you.
The sergeant walks in mid-cleanup.
Let him take the hit
He gets yelled at. You're fine.
{buddy} says you can sell spare issued gear online for good money. 'Nobody counts it,' he says. What do you do?
Two months later, he's under investigation.
Easy money. Your stomach still turns.
theft of government property
NCIS finds the listings. Career over.
{buddy} wants to get matching Raider skull tattoos the night after graduation. Do you join?
It looks great. Your mom does not agree.
Get something subtle
Small and classy. You'll thank yourself at 50.
He calls you boring for a week.
During a land nav event in the desert, your GPS dies and the terrain all looks the same. Water is running low. What do you do?
Map and compass
Old school skills win. You hit every point.
You walk five miles in the wrong direction.
Head for high ground
You spot a landmark and reorient.
The climb drains your water.
Wait for pickup
You fail the event, but you're alive.
During water confidence training, you have to tread water in full kit for 10 minutes. Your arms burn. What do you do?
You finish. The instructor nods.
They pull you out sputtering.
Ditch gear smartly
You drop what you're allowed to. Smart.
You dropped the rifle. Not allowed.
Team Chief Choice
As {rank} you've been asked to take over as team chief. It means more paperwork and less trigger time. Do you accept?
Your team trusts you. You lose sleep and gain gray hairs.
You keep shooting, but the command remembers.
Accept with conditions
Your CO agrees to keep you in the field.
'This isn't a negotiation, {rank}.'
Training the Partner NCOs
Partner force NCOs in {country} defer every decision to their officers. You want them leading. How do you build that?
Run NCO-led drills
A partner sergeant runs a perfect patrol. Huge win.
Their officers feel undermined and shut it down.
Work through their officers
Slow but lasting. The officers buy in.
Progress is glacial.
Things work while you're there. Not after.
Corrupt Partner Commander
You discover the partner force commander in {country} is selling fuel you provided on the black market. What's your move?
Your command addresses it diplomatically. He's replaced.
Nothing happens. He knows you reported him.
He stops. Respect earned.
He freezes your team out of all operations.
The mission continues. Your conscience doesn't sleep well.
Direct Action Raid
Night raid on a compound in {country}. The breach charge fails to fire. Dogs are barking. Your team is stacked at the door. What now?
Mechanical breach
The door gives on the third hit. Target captured.
Someone inside fires through the door.
Find another entry
Window entry catches them totally off guard.
The target escapes out the back.
Re-prime the charge
Second charge works. Clean raid.
The delay gives them time to prepare.
Wait for better ID
He turns. Confirmed match. Clean capture.
He drives off. Window lost.
Move now
It's him. The team takes him without a shot.
Wrong man. A very awkward release and apology.
Ask for higher guidance
Your commander makes the call and owns it.
You've been in a hide site watching a smuggling route for four days. A goat herder is walking straight toward your position. What do you do?
He passes within 10 feet. Never sees you.
His dog finds you. Mission compromised, exfil early.
Quietly relocate
You slip away and set up again.
Rock slide. He definitely heard that.
Call early exfil
Safe, but you lose the observation.
Your vehicle convoy is hit by an IED followed by heavy machine gun fire. The lead vehicle is burning with men inside. What do you do?
Pull them out
You drag two men from the flames under fire.
You're hit reaching the vehicle.
Suppress the gun
Your fire silences the gun. Others pull the men free.
A round finds you behind the turret.
Jets arrive. The enemy breaks off.
Air is 20 minutes out. Too long.
Silver Star Moment
Your team is overrun at an outpost. You're the senior Marine left standing. Ammunition is low. How do you fight?
Your counterattack shatters the assault. The outpost holds.
killed defending an outpost
You're cut down leading the charge.
Consolidate and hold
You hold until the QRF arrives.
You hold, but take shrapnel.
Everyone gets out alive.
The retreat is chaotic. Equipment is left behind.
Medevac Under Fire
{buddy} is badly hit. The medevac bird won't land until the LZ is secured. You have three Marines and a partner squad. What do you do?
Push the perimeter
LZ goes cold. {buddy} makes it out.
You take a round securing it.
Carry him to an alternate LZ
A 600-meter carry. He lives.
He doesn't make it. You carry that forever.
Smoke and pray
The pilots come in anyway. Legends.
The bird takes fire and waves off.
After a firefight, you find a civilian was killed in crossfire. The partner force wants to leave it out of the report. What do you do?
Report it accurately
It's painful, but right. The family gets compensation.
Go along with them
Nobody asks questions.
false official statement
A drone feed contradicts the report. Investigation.
PTSD Creeping In
Since your last deployment, fireworks make you hit the ground and you barely sleep. Your spouse is worried. What do you do?
See a counselor
It's hard to talk, but it helps. Sleep slowly returns.
It works for a night. Then it doesn't.
He's been through the same. You aren't alone.
He changes the subject. He's not ready either.
You've deployed three times in five years. Your spouse says they feel like a single parent. They want you to consider leaving. What do you do?
Request a stateside billet
Instructor duty. Home every night. Your family breathes.
Promise to make it work
You put in the effort. Things improve.
Divorce papers arrive mid-deployment.
Couples counseling
Military OneSource helps. You both listen better.
Sessions keep getting canceled for training.
A new team commander wants to skip rehearsals before a live mission. Your team is uneasy. As senior enlisted, what do you do?
Push back privately
He listens. Rehearsals happen. Mission goes clean.
He overrules you. The mission gets messy.
Go over his head
The company commander intervenes.
You've made an enemy for the rest of the tour.
Run them anyway
Your team rehearses on their own time. He comes around.
He calls it insubordination.
Mentor a Young Raider
A new CSO on your team keeps struggling on the range and is losing confidence. The others are mocking him. What do you do?
Coach him one-on-one
Within a month he's outshooting the mockers.
He improves a little. It's a start.
Shut the mocking down
The team gets the message. Morale improves.
Let him sink or swim
He requests a transfer out. Wasted talent.
You're range safety officer for a demolitions range. A junior Marine sets a charge with the wrong time fuse length. What do you do?
Stop everything
You catch it before anyone gets hurt. Teaching moment.
Fix it quietly
Problem solved without drama.
The charge goes early while you work on it.
{buddy} shows up to morning formation smelling like a brewery for the third time this month. What do you do?
Get him help
He enters a program. He's grateful years later.
He feels betrayed and won't talk to you.
Cover for him
He gets his act together. This time.
He gets a DUI. Your cover-up comes out.
By the book. He's off the team.
Interpreter's Visa
Your interpreter in {country} has saved your life twice. His family is getting threats. His special visa is stuck in paperwork. What do you do?
Write letters, push hard
Months later, he lands in the US. He sends a photo of his kids.
The visa is still pending. You stop sleeping well.
Call your congressman
Their office expedites it.
Your chain of command is annoyed you went outside.
Accept it's out of your hands
You never hear from him again.
You're leading a combat rubber raiding craft insertion. The swells are bigger than forecast and the engine sputters. What do you do?
Push on
You hit the beach on time, soaked.
The boat flips in the surf. Gear lost.
Abort and reschedule
Nobody likes it, but nobody drowns.
Paddle in
Silent and exhausting. It works.
You miss the window by an hour.
Night HALO jump into {country}. At 25,000 feet your oxygen mask feels loose. The green light is on. What do you do?
Tighten and go
Seal holds. Perfect canopy flight to the DZ.
Hypoxia hits in freefall. You barely pull in time.
Sit this pass out
You jump on the second pass and land miles from the team.
Swap masks with the safety
Quick swap. Clean jump.
The swap takes too long. Jumpmaster is furious.
Your unit wants you for another rotation. You've been home seven months. Your knees are shot and your kid's in kindergarten. What do you do?
The team needs your experience. Your kid sends drawings.
Ask for a break
Your sergeant major agrees. You coach T-ball.
Request denied. Pack your bags.
Volunteer to instruct
You go to the schoolhouse. Home for dinner.
You catch a few senior guys making a new operator do humiliating things in the team room. They call it 'tradition'. What do you do?
Stop it now
Uncomfortable for a day. It never happens again.
Investigation follows. Some resentment, but it's done.
It becomes a news story months later. Your name comes up.
You're attached to a government agency team in {country}. Their rules are vague and their requests are sketchy. What do you do?
Stick to your ROE
They grumble, but respect your lines.
Great results. No questions asked.
violating rules of engagement
An inspector general report lands on your desk.
Call your commander
Legal sorts it out. Slow but safe.
Your team's assault dog freezes at a doorway and won't go in. The handler is wounded. What do you do?
Trust the dog
Turns out the room was rigged with explosives. Good dog.
The room was empty. Lost precious time.
Clear it yourself
Empty. Fine.
killed by a booby trap
Booby trap.
MARSOC offers a large reenlistment bonus. A defense contractor offers triple your salary. What do you do?
Bonus banked. Back to the team.
Take the contractor job
Big money. You miss the brotherhood within a month.
Negotiate a better billet
Bonus and your choice of assignment.
You get a smaller bonus and a desk job.
After a long patrol, a junior Marine on your team realizes his rifle is missing. It's 2 AM. What do you do?
Search with the whole team
Found in the back of a truck. Crisis averted.
Not found. Investigation, and everyone loses their weekend.
Report immediately
Painful, but the right move. It's found next day.
You're 34 and the young guys are smoking you on the run. Your PFT is this week. How do you prepare?
Train smart
First-class score. Old man strength.
You pull a calf muscle the day before.
Experience gets you through.
Second class score. The young guys never let it go.
Partner soldiers you trained refuse to fight after their pay is stolen by their own officers. An operation starts tomorrow. What do you do?
Push for their pay
You get the money released. They fight hard.
The operation is canceled.
Go without them
Your team does it alone. It works.
You're badly outnumbered.
Inspire them
Your speech actually lands.
Translation loses everything.
A partner soldier has been staring at your team strangely and asking where you sleep. Your gut says something is wrong. What do you do?
Report and tighten security
Counterintelligence finds he's been contacted by insurgents.
False alarm. Rapport takes a small hit.
Watch him yourself
You catch him with a phone full of enemy contacts.
He opens fire during chow.
Dismiss it
Nothing happens.
Insider attack.
Your team's small surveillance drone crashes in a market in {country}. Kids are already picking it up. What do you do?
Go get it
You trade candy for the drone. Diplomacy.
A crowd forms. Tense moment, mission scrubbed.
Remotely wipe it
Data's gone. Kids get a cool toy.
Send the partner force
They handle it smoothly.
They 'lose' the drone. It ends up for sale.
Gunny's Retirement
Your old gunnery sergeant is retiring after 22 years. They ask you to give a speech. What kind of speech?
Funny roast
The whole room is crying laughing.
One joke goes too far. His wife isn't laughing.
Heartfelt tribute
The old man tears up for the first time ever.
He appreciates it. He hates speeches.
Instructor at ITC
You're now an ITC instructor. A student is talented but arrogant and dangerous on the range. Do you drop him?
Drop him
Hard call. The right one.
Give him one more chance
He gets humbled and becomes a great operator.
He has a negligent discharge. Thankfully into the dirt.
Hand it to the board
The board drops him.
Old Wound Flares
The shrapnel in your back starts acting up during a long ruck. You have miles left. What do you do?
Stop and get checked
Smart. Doc gives you meds and light duty.
You finish. It fades.
Something shifts. Surgery time.
You take command of a Marine Special Operations Team. Your team chief has more combat experience than you. How do you lead?
The team chief becomes your closest ally.
Assert authority
The team respects your confidence.
The team quietly decides you're a problem.
Lead from the front in PT
You crush every workout. They notice.
You injure yourself trying too hard.
Intelligence says a bomb-maker is at a house tonight. The approval chain will take 12 hours. You have the team ready now. What do you do?
Wait for approval
By the time it's approved, he's gone. But you followed the rules.
Push for emergency approval
Approved in an hour. Target captured.
Denied. Higher wants more intel.
Success. Nobody asks too many questions.
dereliction of duty
Investigated. Relieved of command.
The US ambassador in {country} is nervous about your team's operations. She wants fewer raids. How do you respond?
Explain the mission
She becomes a supporter.
She calls your commander to complain.
Shift to training focus
Fewer raids, more partner growth. Everyone's happy.
Ignore her
Your team gets restricted to base. Ouch.
A strike could kill a key militant leader, but there's a chance children are in the building. You have authority. What's your call?
